evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Multi-function Chinese Character Database）
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析；十字形義源流
evidence.text: The database reports oracle-bone and early bronze 十 as a vertical stroke 丨, and records several competing origin accounts: a needle-shaped graph borrowed for the numeral (attributed to 裘錫圭), a straightened stroke used to distinguish ten from 一, a staff, joined upright palms, and a knotted cord. It says some mid-Western Zhou bronze forms add a central dot, which later extends into a short horizontal stroke. These are source-reported proposals and descriptions; the database’s account does not independently establish the depicted needle’s name or pronunciation.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：十

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Multi-function Chinese Character Database）
evidence.field: 甲骨文用例；金文、戰國竹簡用例
evidence.text: The entry reports oracle-bone numeral uses including 合集1654 十月, 合集110反 奠入十 (ten turtle plastrons), and 合集29572 十牢. It also gives a bronze inscription example with 十七年 and a Warring States bamboo-slip example from 清華簡二《繫年》簡3 with 十又四年. These are reported early numeral uses, not demonstrated first attestations; the entry does not establish an early “complete/perfect” sense.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：十

evidence.text: The Shuowen entry gives 十 as 數之具也 and explains 一 as east–west and 丨 as north–south, completing four directions and the center. This is the Han dictionary’s historical explanation, not direct evidence of the graph’s original motivation.
evidence.kind: primary historical dictionary text in modern transcription
evidence.title: 说文解字/03 - 维基文库

evidence.field: File description; source attribution; permission; original-file link
evidence.text: The file description identifies 十-oracle.svg as a modern vector depiction of 十 in Shang oracle script style. It attributes the source glyph to Academia Sinica’s 小學堂 database (record 41.EC21; note 鐵42.1合10966) and marks the file CC0/public domain. Its original-file link resolves to https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/12/%E5%8D%81-oracle.svg. This is a modern redraw, not a photograph or direct scan of an ancient artifact.
evidence.title: File:十-oracle.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: File description; source attribution; permission; original-file link
evidence.text: The file description identifies 十-seal.svg as a modern vector depiction of 十 in Shuowen seal-script style. It names Academia Sinica’s 小學堂 record 27.5341 as one source and marks the file CC0/public domain; its exact original-file link is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/72/%E5%8D%81-seal.svg. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image.
evidence.title: File:十-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: Local primary-reading rows supplied with the research packet; official Unicode Unihan record attempted
evidence.field: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, kMandarin row 十; sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, 十 row (MC and OC columns)
evidence.text: The supplied local rows give Unihan kMandarin 十 = shí and Baxter–Sagart 2014 十: MC dzyip, OC *t.[g]əp, gloss “ten.” These exact local readings corroborate the repository metadata only. The official Unicode character record was attempted but could not be opened, so no externally inspected Unihan page is claimed. No 十 sound component is established here.
evidence.kind: local primary-reading cross-check with upstream access failure
evidence.title: Unicode Unihan character record for U+5341

search_audit.query: 十 甲骨文 金文 字形 演变 小學堂; 十 Shuowen oracle bone numeral paleography needle 針 etymology; site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File 十-seal.svg Shuowen Seal Radical 054.svg
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the CUHK character analysis, Wiktionary summary, Commons seal file description, and Shuowen transcription. The official Unicode page was inaccessible. A Commons search result for the exact seal-radical filename produced an internal error.

Inspected exact Commons description page and confirmed its original-file URL and CC0/public-domain notice. Direct image fetch was attempted through the Commons original-file link but returned a cache miss in the web tool.

Search did not independently return the glyph assets; exact direct URLs had already been obtained from the inspected Commons description pages, whose original-file links failed to fetch in the web tool.

gaps: The earliest depicted referent remains disputed: the sources report numeral-mark, needle, staff, joined-palms, and knotted-cord proposals. The needle proposal does not establish the depicted object’s original name or pronunciation, nor a separately attested early word for that object matching the numeral word; reconstructions alone cannot prove the borrowing.

The form sequence is supported by descriptions and catalog-linked modern redrawings, but no original artifact photograph or direct paleographic catalogue record was visually inspected here. The proposed vector glyphs should be treated as modern redrawings of historical forms.

No exact earliest attestation for the numeral word is established. The reported oracle-bone numerals are early attestations, with the earliest among the examples cited here not independently dated in this research pass. The sequence of modern dictionary glosses does not establish chronology.

The supplied glosses ‘complete; perfect’ and ‘tenth’ are not evidence of their earliest use. ‘Tenth’ is seen in an oracle-bone example 十月, but this does not prove when an ordinal sense first arose. An early ‘complete/perfect’ sense was not established.

No phonetic component is proposed for 十, so no component-host sound array is warranted. The needle theory is a whole-graph borrowing hypothesis and remains unproven; it should not be conflated with a phonetic component analysis.
The official Unicode Unihan record attempt failed; local readings are retained as local-row provenance, not external verification. No exact local row for 針 was supplied or checked.
No bulk-reuse license review was done for recurring paleographic databases. This pass uses concise paraphrases and character-specific Commons image pages; no local text extract is recommended.

items.period: Shang period, as labeled by the source
items.tradition: Shang oracle-bone script; modern vector redraw attributed to 小學堂 record 41.EC21 (catalog note 鐵42.1合10966)
items.caption: A modern redraw of an oracle-script form catalogued for 十. Paleographic descriptions report early forms as a vertical stroke; the exact referent of that stroke is disputed.
items.alt: Modern black vector rendering of a single-stroke Shang oracle-script form labeled 十.
items.selection_reason: Shows the early vertical-stroke form relevant to the supported graphic account while avoiding a claim that the mark depicts a needle or another named object.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition; transmitted Han-dictionary form, not a securely dated artifact image
items.tradition: Shuowen seal script; modern vector redraw attributed in part to 小學堂 record 27.5341
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 十 in the Shuowen seal style. Compare the established seal-form convention with descriptions of earlier vertical-stroke forms.
items.alt: Modern black vector rendering of 十 in a seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: Provides a later conventional form for comparison with the oracle-script redraw; the source explicitly identifies it as a modern vector representation rather than an artifact photograph.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page.

limitations.text: The direct image endpoints were taken from the inspected Commons description pages, but the web tool returned cache-miss errors when fetching them. Candidate identity and rights are supported by those description pages; pixels were not inspected in this research stage.
No selected image is an original artifact photograph; both proposed images are modern digital redrawings of script forms.
